t: You are on platform 1 at Paddington station, looking at the Great Western Railway War Memorial. It commemorates the 2,500 company employees killed in the First World War. About a third of the railway's workforce of almost 80,000 went to fight, with their jobs guaranteed, and the company gave its workshops over to making munitions. The sculptor was Charles Sargeant Jagger, who also made the Royal Artillery Memorial at Hyde Park Corner. The architect Thomas Tait worked with him. Jagger once threatened to resign after some officials kept pushing for a different design.
